memory_candidates.content: When a source-store doc/skill file exceeds a byte ceiling, prefer a restatement-to-pointer trim over cutting operational content: grep the candidate paragraph's facts against the doc(s) it already points to (e.g. an architecture doc or a standards file); if every fact is already fully stated there, collapse the local paragraph to a short operational statement + pointer. Verify no regression by grep-checking that the specific operational instructions/code paths referenced by tests or other agents remain present after the trim, and re-measure with wc -c after each edit rather than estimating.

In a multi-task /orchestrate batch, a shared eager-loaded file (e.g. merge-sources/claudemd.md feeding predicted CLAUDE.md, or a shared command file) can go from measured-under-baseline to measured-over-baseline mid-dispatch because a concurrently-dispatched sibling task lands its own commits to that file. Attribute via `git log --oneline` / `git show <sha> --stat` on the specific paths before touching any shared config value (like a regression baseline). If the growth is the sibling's own declared file_scope work, do not silently absorb it by moving the baseline/ceiling in your own task -- document the attribution with evidence and leave it for the sibling's own scope or a dedicated follow-up.

A verify-deploy.sh-based fixture test suite that spins up its own fixture and invokes verify-deploy.sh --skip-slow multiple times (e.g. test-verify-deploy-context-budget.sh) can easily exceed 150s in foreground; use the Bash tool's run_in_background with an 8+ minute timeout and poll the redirected log file for a sentinel line (e.g. an explicit 'EXITCODE=' appended after the command) rather than relying on a short foreground timeout, which truncates output mid-run and produces a misleadingly short 1-line log.
